problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z),y,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=1+{z}^{2}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z),0⟩,\,∇f=⟨0,0,2z⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(\pi ,1,0).$

feedback.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨y\operatorname{ln}⁡x,0,z⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=\frac{x}{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩,\,∇f=⟨\frac{1}{y},-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,3).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}} & 0 \\ y\operatorname{ln}⁡x & 0 & z\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}(z)-0(0)]i-[\frac{1}{y}(z)-0(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]j+[\frac{1}{y}(0)-(-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}})(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)]k \\  & =-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}}\,i-\frac{z}{y}\,j+\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}\,k \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =\frac{x}{y}⟨0,0,-\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,-\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩+⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{y}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{xz}{{y}^{2}},-\frac{z}{y},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,3) & =⟨-\frac{1(3)}{(1)^{2}},-\frac{3}{1},0⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-3,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
